title: HPI-CT: Healthcare Program Integrity Control Toolkit
description:
HPI-CT is a free, open toolkit that helps healthcare payers, providers and program-integrity agencies find and close the internal-control gaps that fraud, waste and abuse exploit, before payment. Aligned to the GAO Green Book (2025) and cross-referenced to COSO by principle number.

It includes 173 workflow-integrated controls (79 preventive, 87 detective, 7 corrective) across 10 modules, a 247-question evidence-anchored self-assessment mapped to the Green Book's five components and seventeen principles, a control-failure diagnosis matrix, a regulatory rules dictionary, a data-source registry, and de-identified case exemplars distilled from 877 coded U.S. DOJ healthcare-fraud enforcement actions (2023–2026). The published tier carries 871 cases in 21 categories plus 9 state-derived patterns; the 21 categories name the kind of control that failed in the case base's own shorthand, and only the 9 state patterns link to controls in the library. It also includes 128 reference detection tests, tested on synthetic data only. The toolkit runs entirely offline in a browser, no server, no account, and nothing you type leaves your machine.

Code, including the SQL in the detection tests, is licensed MIT; content and data CC BY 4.0. Embedded third-party libraries keep their own MIT licenses (see THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md). Advisory only: it recommends controls and decides nothing. All case references are allegations from public sources and defendants are presumed innocent. Created and maintained by Nicholas Nyarko in a personal capacity from public sources. Screening of the case base and checking of citations and detection tests were done with AI agents on one model; this is internal checking, not independent review.
notes: Correction and extension release. The case base was re-screened against a written inclusion rule (1,586 rows to 877 counted), case figures and citations were recomputed and corrected, a Preclusion List control and assessment question were added, and 128 reference detection tests were added.
